title: Effective normalized models for integral pullback and scalar realization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L\subset M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, allowing equality, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizers $\varpi_F$, and $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes have $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites put $R_{F,X}=\lim_n(A_{F,n})_X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\mathscr S_F(X)$ for the abelian category of strict quotient-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, $\mathcal R_{F,X}$ for derived reduction and $\mathcal L_{F,X}=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for realization [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A system $C$ is normalized when $C_m\otimes^L_{A_{F,m}}A_{F,n}\to C_n$ is an isomorphism for $m\geq n$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower].

Use the whole-system pullbacks $U_{f,F}$, scalar changes $S_{L/E,X}$ and their specified comparison maps [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], and the completed pullbacks $\widehat U_{f,F}=Lf_F^*$ and scalar extensions $\widehat S_{L/E,X}=T_{L/E,X}$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

There exist simultaneous Roos, pullback and scalar realization models with precisely the representative normalization of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], for every scheme, scheme map and coefficient inclusion under consideration. More explicitly, their primitive realization isomorphisms are
$$\widehat U_{f,F}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{F,X}U_{f,F}\mathcal R_{F,Y}K,\qquad
\widehat S_{L/E,X}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_{L,X}S_{L/E,X}\mathcal R_{E,X}K.$$
On every flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], these are the defining quotient-complex realizations with the actual transitions of $P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}(A_{F,n})_Y$; simultaneous scalar reassociation is $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$. The initial completion map has its quotient-map component in the unshifted Roos product and zero component in the shifted product.

Let $e_C:\mathcal R\mathcal LC\to C$ be the whole-system reduction/realization counit. It is the levelwise derived-change-of-rings adjunct of $\epsilon_{\operatorname{Res}C}:\Delta R\lim\operatorname{Res}C\to\operatorname{Res}C$, normalized on a K-injective tower resolution $q:\operatorname{Res}C\to I$ by $[q]^{-1}\circ(\Delta\lim I\to I)$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For a constructible derived-complete $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the systems $U_{f,E}\mathcal R_EK$ and $S_{L/E,Y}\mathcal R_EK$ are normalized, their realizations belong to $\mathcal C_E(X)$ and $\mathcal C_L(Y)$ respectively, and $e$ at these systems is an isomorphism in the derived category of the entire quotient diagram. The completion unit of $K$ is an isomorphism as well. The counit and the primitive model isomorphisms descend naturally through changes of flat-term K-flat representatives, K-injective tower resolutions and common refinements, with the quotient-transition maps retained. No finite Tor-amplitude or flatness of $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,n}$ is assumed.

proof.text: For each scheme $W$ and coefficient field $F$, form the same strict-tower cone functor $H(D)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_D)[-1]$ on restricted quotient-system complexes. Countable products of $R_{F,W}$-modules are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] supplies a natural isomorphism $\rho_D:H(D)\simeq R\lim D$ on the entire derived tower category. Use this functor and this comparison throughout. Its specified inclusion of an ordinary limit into the cone is the limit tuple in the unshifted product and zero in the shifted product. Its comparison with a K-injective tower model is independent of the resolution. This constructs the Roos part of the requested interface, including its normalization, before choosing any pullback or scalar representatives.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, K-injective limit and product-cone computation; strict normalization as specified in the cited comparison node

proof.text:
Use the specified derived adjunction $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], rather than selecting maps independently at its levels. For a restricted tower $D=\operatorname{Res}C$ and a K-injective resolution $q:D\to I$, compute $R\lim D$ by $\lim I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its limit projections are represented, simultaneously as a map of towers, by
$$\Delta\lim I\longrightarrow I\xrightarrow{[q]^{-1}}D.$$
Indeed the first map is the ordinary limit cone; composing its $n$th projection with $[q_n]^{-1}$ is precisely the total-limit projection to $D_n$. The evaluation of $e_C$ is its scalar-extension adjunct by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. This gives the formula in the statement for $\epsilon_D$, with the indicated order of composition. The whole-system counit, including its quotient transitions, already exists in that adjunction; the calculation identifies its evaluated adjuncts and does not attempt to construct a system map from a collection of unrelated derived maps.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, limit of a K-injective tower; simultaneous adjunction specified by the cited system-calculus node

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its quotient complexes $P_{F,n}=P\otimes_{R_{F,Y}}(A_{F,n})_Y$ are flat-term K-flat over the quotient rings by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. They represent $\mathcal R_{F,Y}K$ with the actual quotient maps by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The whole-system inverse image of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems] is represented here by $(f_n^*P_{F,n})_n$: finite constant-coefficient inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], and its transitions are the images of $P_{F,m}\to P_{F,n}$. The defining formula of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] for $\widehat U_{f,F}K$ is exactly the Roos realization of this restricted tower. Apply $\rho$ of Step 1 to this same tower. This gives the primitive isomorphism $\widehat U_{f,F}K\simeq\mathcal L_{F,X}U_{f,F}\mathcal R_{F,Y}K$ with the prescribed quotient-complex representative, without interchanging inverse image with an infinite product.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (5), completed pullback as quotient realization; representative construction uses sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS and 0G7E

proof.text: For a coefficient inclusion $E\subset L$ and the same kind of representative $P$, the scalar-changed whole system of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems] is represented at level $n$ by $(P\otimes_{R_{E,X}}(A_{E,n})_X)\otimes_{(A_{E,n})_X}(A_{L,n})_X$. The simultaneous scalar-association isomorphism in [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] identifies this, with all its transitions, with $P\otimes_{R_{E,X}}(A_{L,n})_X$ by $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$. These tensors compute derived extension even for ramified inclusions: the first quotient complex is K-flat over $(A_{E,n})_X$ by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. By [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], its Roos cone is the defining value of $\widehat S_{L/E,X}K$. Compose the identification of cones with $\rho$ of Step 1 to obtain the scalar primitive isomorphism. The association map commutes with $n+1\to n$ since both paths send $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes\overline{ab}$. For a third field $M$, both associations send $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes abc$; for equal fields multiplication gives the unit comparison. Hence all inclusions use the same simultaneous quotient normalization.

source.place: Tags 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, and 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; scalar quotient construction in the cited reduction-model node

proof.text:
For the initial completion map use the actual adjunction unit, not an arbitrary map having its levelwise projections. On $P\to K$ the strict quotient augmentation is
$$v_P:P\longrightarrow H(\operatorname{Res}\mathcal RP),\qquad z\longmapsto(0,(z\otimes1)_n),$$
where the shifted product is written first. It is a chain map because each quotient transition sends $z\otimes1$ to $z\otimes1$, so $(1-s)(z\otimes1)_n=0$. The whole-morphism equality $u_K=\rho[v_P][P\to K]^{-1}$, including its resolution-independent interpretation, is exactly [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model]. This gives the zero shifted coordinate required by [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models].

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; actual quotient-unit identification supplied by the cited strict-quotient-model node

proof.text: The reduction system $\mathcal R_EK$ is normalized by [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps]. Its whole-system inverse image is normalized by the inverse-image clause of [lem-pur-system-normalized-tensor-closure], applied to the pro-etale inverse-image morphism and the constant quotient coefficient sheaves. Their identification with the target constant sheaves is part of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The scalar system $S_{L/E,Y}\mathcal R_EK$ is normalized by [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model], which applies to arbitrary ambient $K$ and explicitly permits ramification. Apply [lem-pur-normalized-actual-reconstruction-maps] separately over $E$ on $X$ and over $L$ on $Y$: both realizations are derived complete and their actual counits $e$ are isomorphisms in the derived categories of whole strict systems. When $K$ is derived complete the same node makes its actual unit $u_K$ invertible. Thus effectivity concerns the actual maps fixed in Steps 2 and 5; it is not inferred merely from the existence of some levelwise isomorphisms.

source.place: Final sentence, Frobenius transport through the common-stage category: normalized integral realization; generic reconstruction and inverse-image tools are used as stated

proof.text: Now let $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] the completed pullback $\widehat U_{f,E}K$ belongs to $\mathcal C_E(X)$. By [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] the completed scalar extension $\widehat S_{L/E,Y}K$ belongs to $\mathcal C_L(Y)$. The primitive isomorphisms constructed in Steps 3 and 4 identify these with the two realizations in the statement. Hence those realizations have the required bounded constructible reductions and the single uniform cohomological interval of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. These two preservation statements have precisely the arbitrary scheme-map and finite coefficient-extension hypotheses in force here. No separate flatness or finite Tor-amplitude assumption on the finite quotient coefficient map is inserted.

source.place: Final sentence, integral comparison underlying common finite coefficient stages; constructibility is supplied by the cited preservation theorems

proof.text: Finally descend the construction simultaneously. A comparison between flat-term K-flat representatives is sent to a quasi-isomorphism of pullback Roos complexes by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], and to one of scalar Roos complexes by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Both nodes give descended functors and canonical comparison isomorphisms compatible with every K-flat representative. Scalar association is independent of the representative as a coherent system comparison by [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model]. The comparison $\rho$ is natural on the derived category of whole towers and independent of K-injective resolutions by [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Thus the primitive maps are composites of these natural comparisons, so commute with every change of representative and with a common refinement. The counit is already a natural transformation of whole-system derived functors, by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; its representative formula in Step 2 computes that fixed transformation on any resolution. Consequently changing a tower resolution also leaves it unchanged. All these comparisons are formed before the limit from strict quotient maps or from functors of the whole diagram. They retain every quotient transition. Use this single Roos functor, this fixed adjunction, and these comparisons for each field and scheme; the generator identities in Step 4 hold on any simultaneous representative and survive localization. They therefore give the simultaneous models of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], with the asserted natural descent.
